One immediate thing: "Audio" is almost always uncountable, so it's very unusual to speak of "audios"

If plural is absolutely necessary the better choice would be "sounds" IMO

On second thought yes "sound" would be a better word to use for this feature, *usually* "audio" is used more generally and "sound" more specifically for discrete instances, even in computing related topics
Hover sounds for elements inside of popup menu and tree would be convenient

Would this be compatible with third party audio solutions like the [Wwise plugin](https://github.com/alessandrofama/wwise-godot-integration) or FMOD? They would need to expose a AudioStream inherited resource for their events or something like that? Wwise doesn't really have an equivalent of AudioStreamPlayer it could return afaik, it's the point of having an audio middleware
Thanks for the awesome work :)

One minor concern is the need to provide the ability to change the control's state (grab focus, toggle a button) without triggering a sound effect. This might be necessary if you want to update the UI from code but don't want to produce sounds that aren't initiated by the user. For example, we could add a `grab_focus_no_sound()` method, similar to the existing `BaseButton.set_pressed_no_signal()` and `Range.set_value_no_signal()` methods. Note that `set_pressed_*()` will likely now require a list of arguments or a bitmask (whether to emit a signal and play a sound).

Another concern is how suitable this system will be for people who want perfect timing for sound effects. For example, sound effects for typing and popup menus depend on the cursor delay and the appearance of the popup window.

I've pushed an update that renames `audio(s)` to `sound(s)`, to address the issue with the wording.

**Edit:** This also adds sound events for PopupMenu, ItemList and Tree hover/focus changes.

> Would this be compatible with third party audio solutions like the [Wwise plugin](https://github.com/alessandrofama/wwise-godot-integration?rgh-link-date=2025-10-11T10%3A14%3A53Z) or FMOD? They would need to expose a AudioStream inherited resource for their events or something like that? Wwise doesn't really have an equivalent of AudioStreamPlayer it could return afaik, it's the point of having an audio middleware Thanks for the awesome work :)

Unfortunately, no, as the audio playback behavior is hardcoded. If you can think of way for a plugin to register a custom approach to audio playback, I could consider it for a future PR.

I expect audio playback will still work even if it doesn't go through the middleware, but you won't be able to make use of the middleware's functionality for theme sounds.

> One minor concern is the need to provide the ability to change the control's state (grab focus, toggle a button) without triggering a sound effect.

Programmatic calls currently don't trigger sound effects. I believe this is the better option overall, even if we may want to have a way to do so in the future (I'd prefer leaving it for a future PR). I've added a <kbd>G</kbd> key binding to the control gallery demo so you can check this behavior; when pressed, it focuses the first button, similar to the `grab_focus()` call in `_ready()`.

Likewise, this means https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106985 wouldn't play a focus sound.

I applied most suggestions and made some extra improvements:

- I added `text_change_rejected_sound` to TextEdit, which plays when pressing <kbd>Backspace</kbd> when there is no text. I also made LineEdit's existing `text_change_rejected_sound` play in the same scenario.
- ColorPicker now plays drag begin/end sounds from Slider, and a button press sound from BaseButton when clicking the "revert to old color" icon. This reuses existing theme items, which means no theme configuration is needed.

The editor is able to play sound otherwise. > - SpinBox does not have any sounds for dragging the value. Added. This reuses Slider's `drag_started_sound` and `drag_ended_sound` automatically, no configuration is needed. > - ColorPicker could have sounds for keyboard navigation. Also maybe for picking the from screen? I can reuse the BaseButton press sound for this, but I'm having issues with the screen picker on Linux/X11 (pressing the button does nothing, regardless of whether the project is running in single-window mode). > - LineEdit/TextEdit could get sounds for moving the caret. Added (using a new `caret_moved_sound` theme item in LineEdit and TextEdit). I've updated the testing project in OP to add those theme items. > - Tree has various internal controls, like text boxes, buttons, checkboxes, combo boxes and sliders. Though not sure if it's worth it adding sound for every of them. We can reuse existing theme items so that people don't need to configure more theme items, but it's a lot of work to add calls where needed. I'll leave this for a future PR, as it can be done in a fully backwards-compatible manner. > - TabContainer (TabBar) has no sound for keyboard navigation. Fixed.

> feel free to suggest extra actions that could benefit from sounds

- Sliders in games often play sound repeatedly at set value interval when adjusted (when you drag it with mouse)
- Games often play sound effects on navigation when you go between menu screens or when pop-ups appear. On SteamOS (and other console OSes) when you navigate between screens there are different sounds depending on what screen or popup you opened. Playing sounds on node visibility changes could be out of scope of this PR, and also even if it was on the table there would need to be some config flexibility to sync the timing of the sound to the animation. However if this is meant to be a comprehensive solution to UI sounds it's probably worth thinking about what the intended final full ui sound solution would look like and how it all fits with this PR (sorry it this was already discussed somewhere, I wasn't keeping track)

I've just implemented support for runtime changes of the GUI theme bus using the `project_settings_changed` signal. This means you can change it while in the editor and it'll reflect in the editor's theme preview immediately.

Rebased and tested again, it works as expected. I've made some additional changes: - ScrollBar can now play sounds (same as Slider: drag started/ended, value changed, rejected value change when already at the beginning/end). - Slider now plays a different sound when a change is rejected, similar to LineEdit and TextEdit. - LineEdit and TextEdit now play their respective "change rejected" sound when pressing Delete while at the end of the text, similar to pressing Backspace when at the beginning. - LineEdit and TextEdit now play a "caret move rejected" sound when the caret doesn't actually move as a result of keyboard input, e.g. because it's already at the beginning/end of the text. - This handles multiple carets in TextEdit too (sound only plays once for all carets, and the normal sound is played if at least one caret moves). - As usual, both "change rejected" sounds above can be left empty if you don't want any sound to play in those situations. I've updated the testing project to account for the new sounds. Something else I noticed is that the theme editor doesn't offer abstract classes in its list, so you can't easily add the sound theme items for Slider or Scrollbar: This should probably be addressed in a separate PR.

> Maybe caret move rejected sound should not be played for echo events? I think it can get annoying the way it continuously plays the rejected sound when holding the button (at least with the sounds in the demo) and it doesn't help convey more information than if it just played the sound once.
